channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Four metals, third session: gold $4,157.80, silver up 3.27%
item.description: At 5:58am New York gold bid $4,157.80, up 1.99%, silver $61.35, up 3.27%, platinum $1,747.00, up 1.10% and palladium $1,355.00, up 1.96%. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.8.

item.title: ₹1,45,359 and rising: India confirms the metals turn at home
item.description: October gold on the MCX rose 0.73% to ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams and September silver 1.13% to ₹2,24,109 a kilo. Indian jewellery demand fell 19% in the first quarter and 15% in the second.

item.title: Twenty percent in June: Hong Kong's fourteenth month up
item.description: Jewellery, watches and clocks took HK$5.49 billion in June, up 20% year on year, inside overall retail of HK$31.49 billion, up 5%. First-half hard luxury rose 25% to HK$31.07 billion.

item.title: Six months empty: Pandora hands North America to a beauty CEO
item.description: André Branch becomes president of Pandora's North America cluster on 15 August, a seat vacant since Luciano Rodembusch left in February. He arrives from R.E.M. Beauty, with two decades in consumer brands and none in jewellery.

item.title: Fifty percent on fixed price: how Luk Fook outran the gold price
item.description: Net profit rose 88.7% to HK$2.015 billion in the year to 31 March, on revenue up 29% to HK$17.21 billion. Fixed-price jewellery sales rose 50.5% against 22% for gold and platinum by weight.

item.title: Eighty percent to the consumer: the NDC changes the subject
item.description: Amber Pepper told a GJEPC meeting in Mumbai that at least 80% of Natural Diamond Council advertising now goes to consumers, with a desire index baseline due in September and a trust mark to be inscribed on stones.

item.title: $230,000 bid on a moonwalker's Omega: Joopiter opens its watch room
item.description: Keeping Measure, the first sale from Joopiter's watch department, closes on a rolling basis through 11 August. The top lot, an Omega Speedmaster engraved for Alan Bean, carries a $250,000 to $350,000 estimate against a $230,000 bid.

item.title: The 1-carat stops falling: polished's best month since the tariffs
item.description: July ended a thirteen-month slide in the 1-carat index at flat, while 0.30-carat rose 1.6%, 0.50-carat rose 1.8% and 3-carat rose 0.2%. The first month since March 2025 with nothing falling.

item.title: Minus 0.1% for color: pinks rise, blues and yellows slip
item.description: The Fancy Color Research Foundation's second-quarter index moved one tenth of one percent. Pink gained 0.1%, blue lost 0.4%, yellow lost 0.3%. The widest single move in the set was a 1.3% fall in 2-carat blues.

item.title: $633.8 million for the independents, more than LVMH's watches
item.description: EveryWatch puts the first-half secondary market at $10.5 billion, up 37.2%. Independent makers took $633.8 million of it, up 89%, with F.P. Journe alone at $201.6 million on a median sale price of $215,000.

item.title: 1.2 million apply for 1,969 watches, and nobody queued
item.description: Swatch put its MoonSwatch 1969 behind a 32-question online form. More than 1.2 million people completed it for 1,969 pieces at $570, roughly 600 applicants per watch, three months after crowds forced 15 US stores shut.

item.title: 73 lots over a million: the watch auction room reflates
item.description: EveryWatch puts first-half watch auction sales at $680 million, up 45%. Seventy-three lots cleared $1 million against roughly 25 a year earlier, three passed $10 million, and the median watch sold for $5,900.

item.title: Platinum adds 1.7%, gold slips: the white metals lead again
item.description: At 5:59am New York, gold bid $4,048.80, down 0.14%. Platinum is $1,655.00, up 1.72%, palladium $1,266.00, up 1.77%, and silver $58.63, up 0.97%. ADP lands Wednesday, payrolls Friday.

item.title: 1,300 brands and a centenary: Vicenzaoro opens Hall 2
item.description: Vicenzaoro September runs 4 to 8 September with about 1,300 brands from 38 countries, buyers from more than 130, the new Hall 2 in full use and T.Gold moved on site. CIBJO's centenary congress sits inside it.

item.title: $73 million in shoes, and a serial number to collect it
item.description: Vietnamese police have re-scaled the smuggling case this desk reported on July 16. The ring now stands at $73 million of stones, more than 30 detained, and a state-owned retailer holding 3,400 of the diamonds.

item.title: China's gold counter falls to its lowest since 2004
item.description: Chinese gold jewellery demand fell 28% to 50 tonnes in the second quarter, the weakest since 2004, and 30% across the half to 136 tonnes. The value of that demand still rose 11%.

item.title: Silver leads the reopen at $58.05, gold adds 0.29%
item.description: The first session since Friday has gold at $4,053.30, up $11.60, and silver at $58.05, up 1.06%. Platinum is $1,647.00. The ADP report lands midweek and payrolls on Friday.

item.title: Michael Hill adds 2%, and closes eight stores to do it
item.description: Group revenue rose 2% to A$654.7 million in the year to June 28, with same-store sales up 3% and Canada a record 7%. The chain closed eight stores and opened two.

item.title: Shoplifting falls 12.4%, and the fraud desk fills up
item.description: The National Retail Federation's 2026 study has shoplifting incidents down 12.4% and merchandise theft down 8.1%, while 69% of retailers report rising phone scams and 42% report gift-card fraud.

item.title: Nobody has De Beers yet, and there will be no listing
item.description: Anglo American's chief executive says the sale is in its final and hardest phase, that no bidder holds exclusivity, and that a public listing is off the table. Completion is targeted for the second half.

item.title: Zero for Antwerp, and the grown stone pays anyway
item.description: The Section 301 tariffs that took effect on July 24 exempt loose natural diamonds cut in the European Union at 0%, along with coloured stones and natural pearls. Lab-grown diamonds received no exemption anywhere on the list.

item.title: The tender ladder: 100% in Dubai, 75% in Johannesburg
item.description: TAGS cleared 100% of a Zimbabwean parcel and 95% of an Angolan one this summer, but only about 75% of South African goods in Johannesburg. Its latest Dubai sale of large South African stones took $15.2 million at above 80%.

item.title: A record second quarter, the weakest half since 2022
item.description: Central banks bought 289 tonnes of gold in the second quarter, up 62% and a record for any second quarter. The first half still totalled 345 tonnes, the smallest since 2022, because the first quarter collapsed to 57.

item.title: $380 billion: the half-year that cost the most
item.description: Total gold demand held flat at 1,269 tonnes in the second quarter and rose 2% to 2,522 tonnes across the half. In money rather than metal, that half-year set a record near $380 billion.

item.title: Gold opens August at $4,041.70 and waits on payrolls
item.description: No session since Friday's Kitco close of $4,041.70, so the tape carries. The week brings the ADP employment report midweek and non-farm payrolls on Friday, into a metal six weeks into a consolidation.

item.title: NY Now opens today under new owners
item.description: The summer market runs August 2 to 4 at the Javits Center, the first edition since Rockview Management Group bought the show from Emerald. More than 70 exhibitors are new or returning.

item.title: Bain puts jewellery on top of a flat luxury market
item.description: The Bain and Altagamma spring study has personal luxury goods growing 2% to 4% in 2026, reaching €365 to €373 billion after falling to €358 billion last year. Jewellery is named the strongest category.

item.title: Russia bans the word: synthetics lose diamond, carat and natural
item.description: Government Resolution No. 657 of May 30 takes effect on September 1. Tags must say synthetic, weight must be shown in grams rather than carats, and precious, natural, real and eco-friendly are struck from the vocabulary.

item.title: Dubai sets a second Diamond Week for October 26
item.description: DMCC will run the second Dubai Diamond Week from October 26 to 29, with the Italian Exhibition Group co-hosting a sourcing show. The emirate traded a record $41.7 billion and 359.5 million carats last year.

item.title: $4,041.70: gold's first monthly gain since February
item.description: Kitco's Friday close puts gold at $4,041.70, down $60.90 or 1.48% on the day. July still finished about 0.5% higher, ending a four-month losing run, as the dollar rebounded from a six-week low.
